1.why: Every step is a static card layout with no animations, carousels, or modal pop-ups anywhere in the eight screenshots.

2.why: Bold headings and a single high-contrast dark-blue primary button dominate each screen, though the large dark 'Logs' panel competes visually with the actual task area.

3.why: Each screen presents one field and one button so the next action is obvious, but step 1 buries the email field under two dense advisory boxes.

4.why: Password rules are shown on screen and the recovery token is pre-filled at step 3, but the MFA code (246810) appears only in the Logs panel and must be manually carried into the empty verification field.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: The submitted email persists and the recovery token is echoed into the verification field, but there are no saved credentials, account avatars, or other recognisable familiar items.

7.why: Sentences are short and legible, but step 1 uses technical jargon such as 'privacy-neutral test recovery token' and 'account-bound recovery token', and the Logs use small monospace text.

8.why: No error state is shown at all in the eight screenshots—no invalid-token, wrong-code, or weak-password message with remediation guidance.

9.why: Fields have labels and the password rule is stated in prose, but there are no placeholder examples, format hints, or sample values for the email, token, or 6-digit code.

10.why: The single password-then-code path is clearly labelled at each step, but no alternative login choices (biometric/face, passkey, backup method) are offered or explained.

11.why: Each screen exposes exactly one input and one primary button, so the user is never presented with competing options simultaneously.

12.why: Confirmation lines such as 'recovery instructions will be sent securely', the growing Logs list, and the final 'appointment request has been confirmed' clearly report outcomes, though the token-verification step gives no explicit success message.

13.why: Short guidance sits under each heading (e.g., password composition rule, 'Open links only from this hospital site') plus a persistent safety footer tip.

14.why: No back link, 'resend code', 'request a new token', or retry affordance is visible on any step, so recovery from a mistake is not supported in the UI.

15.why: All eight steps reuse the identical header, white rounded card, label-above-field pattern, dark blue button style, Logs panel, and footer note.
